feeds_accelerator_ids.locator: NuMI Neutrino Beam paper, §2 "NuMI Beam Components"
feeds_accelerator_ids.note: No dates: the relationship runs from the Booster's first beam to the present (hull of the two records). Planned: the 400 MeV Linac is to be replaced by the PIP-II linac (accelerator:fermilab-pip-ii); the May 2026 Fermilab plan says that after the 2028-2029 long shutdown "Operation of the current Linac and associated Irradiation Test Area ends" (draft schedule).
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: Protons originate as H− ions in the Linac which accelerates them to 400 MeV. The ions are converted into protons in the Booster where they are accelerated to 8 GeV as 1.6 µs long batches with a 53 MHz bunch spacing.

intervals.label: construction
intervals.locator: Fermilab History and Archives, page 'Accelerator History', section 'Linacs'; start also: article 'The birth of Fermilab'
intervals.note: The news article states the 1 December 1968 groundbreaking was for the linac, the first part of the accelerator complex. No completion date sourced. Recorded as a phase annotation: the source gives the groundbreaking date but no completion, so it marks a milestone rather than an ongoing state. The Fermilab accelerator-history page says the Linac "achieved its design energy of 200 MeV exactly two years later, on December 1, 1970" (another paper dates the first 200 MeV beam to 30 November 1970: arXiv:physics/0008176).
intervals.quote: The groundbreaking for the Linac was on December 1, 1968 and it achieved its design energy of 200 MeV exactly two years later, on December 1, 1970.

intervals.label: operating
intervals.locator: Fermilab History and Archives, page 'Accelerator History', section 'Linacs'
intervals.note: Start is the day the Linac reached its design energy of 200 MeV (1 December 1970). The same page says the Linac was upgraded in the early 1990s to a new design energy of 400 MeV on 4 September 1993 (the 400 MeV machine is the one the NuMI beam paper describes); NuMI beam data taking from 20 May 2005 documents it as operating. The NuMI paper is cited at section 2, PDF p. 6 (see the sources).
intervals.quote: The groundbreaking for the Linac was on December 1, 1968 and it achieved its design energy of 200 MeV exactly two years later, on December 1, 1970.

intervals.note: Start = the day the linac reached its design energy of 200 MeV (see the operating interval). End: the upgrade to 400 MeV was done between Run Ia (ended May 1993) and Run Ib (initiated December 1993); the exact day is not stated.

summary.plain: The first machine in the Fermilab chain: it turns hydrogen ions into a 400-million-electronvolt beam and passes them to the next accelerator.
summary.technical: 201.25 MHz normal-conducting H- linac delivering 400 MeV to the Booster; to be replaced by the 800 MeV PIP-II superconducting linac.
